home.title: Will your skills survive the AI era?
home.subtitle: FutureProof scores every skill you have on two things: how much the job market wants it, and how much AI can already do it. Then it gives you a 4-week plan to close the gaps — in Bangla or English.
home.noSignupNote: No credit card. You can delete everything you upload, any time.
home.step1Body: Upload a PDF or paste your experience. Your name, email and phone are removed before anything is analyzed.
home.step2Body: Every skill is scored on market demand and AI exposure, with the source shown for each number.
home.step3Body: A learning path built only from verified free and low-cost courses, matched to your gaps.
home.trustTitle: Why you can trust these numbers
home.trust1Body: Scores are computed by tested code, never by the AI. The AI only explains and translates.
home.trust2Body: Open any skill to see the data behind it. AI-estimated values are labelled as estimates.
home.trust3Body: Personal details are stripped before analysis. Your CV is deleted automatically after 30 days.

methodology.title: Methodology and data
methodology.subtitle: Every formula, weight, source and limitation behind the Future-Proof Score.
methodology.introBody: A skill is worth investing in when two things are true at once: employers are asking for it, and AI cannot easily do the work behind it. The Future-Proof Score combines those two axes for every skill you have.
methodology.formulaDemand: Demand = 0.7 × percentile rank of the skill's job-posting count + 0.3 × demand trend (rescaled to 0–1)
methodology.formulaExposure: AI exposure = importance-weighted mean exposure across the tasks linked to the skill
methodology.weightsBody: All weights live in one configuration file and are shown here so the code and this page can never disagree.
methodology.dataBody: Task exposure values in this build are rubric estimates, not measurements from a published dataset. Job demand comes from a synthetic posting sample created for development.
methodology.limitation1: The occupation taxonomy is curated for Bangladeshi graduate roles and is not yet the full O*NET database.
methodology.limitation2: Task-to-skill links are keyword-derived heuristics, not authoritative occupational mappings.
methodology.limitation3: Job-demand counts come from a synthetic sample, so absolute demand levels are illustrative.
methodology.limitation4: AI exposure estimates describe today's capabilities. They are estimates, not predictions.
methodology.limitation5: The score reflects skills you listed. Skills you have but did not write down are invisible to it.
methodology.reproducibilityBody: The score is a pure function. The same input always produces the same output, and the scoring engine is covered by unit tests including a fairness test.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.subtitle: What we collect, what leaves the system, and what you can delete.
privacy.scrubBody: Before any analysis, your name, email, phone number, postal address, date of birth, gender, national ID, URLs and institution names are stripped from the text. This is done by tested code, not by a model.
privacy.leavesBody: Only the scrubbed text is sent to the AI provider for skill extraction. Skill names may be sent to an embedding provider for matching. No personal identifiers are shared.
privacy.storageBody: The scrubbed CV text and the analysis result. Uploaded PDF files are not retained; CV records expire after 30 days.
privacy.controlBody: Export everything as JSON, or delete every record tied to you — both available in Settings.
privacy.auditBody: Every AI call is logged with its purpose, model and token counts. The prompt is stored only as a hash; no CV text is ever written to the log.

dash.subtitle: This is the running instance. The figures below are queried from the live data provider on every page load.

problem.title: The problem
problem.subtitle: A composite persona, built from the pattern we kept hearing — not one real person.
problem.body: A final-year student in Dhaka finishes a degree, writes "Microsoft Excel, data entry, report writing" on his CV, and applies to forty jobs. He has no way to know that the tasks behind those three lines are the ones automation is eating first. Career advice reaches him as opinion: "learn AI", "learn coding". Nobody shows him which of his own skills are exposed, or which nearby role his existing skills already half-qualify him for.
problem.callout: "Rahim" is a composite persona used to illustrate the problem. He is not a real user and the numbers in our demo are synthetic.

solution.title: The solution
solution.subtitle: Four steps. The score is arithmetic; the language model only reads and writes prose.

steps.s1d: A CV (PDF, DOCX or TXT, parsed in the browser) or a plain description of what you can do. Nothing is stored unless you ask it to be.
steps.s2d: Names, emails, phone numbers, national IDs and addresses are removed before anything else happens. The model never sees them.
steps.s3d: Each skill is mapped onto a 446-skill taxonomy and scored on demand and AI exposure using published formulas. No model is involved in the arithmetic.
steps.s4d: An LLM writes the explanation and the 90-day plan, but every number it quotes is checked against the computed set — if it invents one, the whole answer is discarded.

arch.title: Architecture
arch.subtitle: One codebase, two deployment modes. Switching from local JSON to Supabase is an environment variable, not a rewrite.
arch.caption: Data flows left to right. The scoring core never calls a model; the language model sits beside it and can only read its output.

scoring.title: Scoring at a glance
scoring.subtitle: The full derivation, with every weight and threshold, is on the methodology page.

ai.title: Where AI is and is not used
ai.subtitle: The honest version. We would rather lose points than claim something the code does not do.

rows.r1h: Structured extraction into a fixed schema, with a deterministic dictionary fallback when no key is present.
rows.r2h: Exact and alias matching first; embeddings only for the residue that the dictionary cannot resolve.
rows.r3h: Pure TypeScript arithmetic over the task-exposure and demand tables. Deterministic and unit-tested.
rows.r4h: Written by an LLM, then verified: any number not present in the computed set discards the entire response.
rows.r5h: Retrieval first, generation second — the model may only recommend courses that were retrieved from the database.
rows.r6h: Interface strings are human-written Bangla and English; the model only handles user-generated text.

mcp.title: MCP server
mcp.subtitle: The same scoring core, exposed over the Model Context Protocol so an assistant can answer with our numbers instead of its own guess.
mcp.t1p: Future-Proof Score, per-skill breakdown, top gaps, safer adjacent roles
mcp.t2p: Posting counts, 30-day trend, demand percentile, AI exposure, verified courses
mcp.t3p: A checkable plain-language breakdown, in English or Bangla
mcp.note: All three tools are read-only, call no language model, work offline, and label synthetic data in every response.
mcp.verify: npm test connects a real MCP client over stdio and runs 19 checks, including determinism.

lifecycle.title: Data lifecycle
lifecycle.subtitle: Collect, normalise, score, explain, delete. Each stage has a rule.

stages.s1d: O*NET-style task and skill data, plus job postings. Public sources only, robots.txt respected, licences recorded per source.
stages.s2d: One canonical skill taxonomy with Bangla aliases, so "এক্সেল" and "Excel" resolve to the same node.
stages.s3d: Deterministic formulas. The same input always yields the same score, which is what makes it auditable.
stages.s4d: An LLM turns the numbers into advice, constrained to the computed values and verified courses.
stages.s5d: CV text is discarded after the response unless the user saves the analysis. Export and delete are self-service.

security.title: Security and privacy
security.subtitle: The shortest honest summary of what we do with your data.

items.i1: Identifiers are stripped before the text leaves the server for a model call.
items.i2: CV text is not persisted by default; saved analyses are owned by a key held in your browser.
items.i3: No secrets reach the client — only NEXT_PUBLIC_* values are exposed.
items.i4: Per-IP rate limiting, strict security headers, and a Content Security Policy.
items.i5: Export and delete are self-service from the settings page.
